question: In which city is the sculptural panel of "Descent of the Ganges" located?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahabalipuram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Descent of the Ganges" is a famous sculptural panel located in **Mahabalipuram**, Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• It is one of the largest open-air rock reliefs in the world, measuring approximately 29 meters in length and 13 meters in height.
 
• The panel depicts the story of the sacred river Ganges descending to Earth from the heavens, as per Hindu mythology, with the help of Lord Shiva.
 
• This magnificent sculpture showcases intricate carvings of gods, demigods, animals, and other celestial beings, representing the divine event.
 
• Mahabalipuram, also known as Mamallapuram, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its group of monuments including rock-cut caves, temples, and sculptures from the Pallava period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ellora:**

 
 
• Ellora is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Maharashtra, India, and is famous for its rock-cut caves dating back to the Rashtrakuta dynasty.
 
• It consists of 34 caves, including Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain temples and monasteries, showcasing India's religious diversity.
 
• The most notable structure is the Kailasa Temple (Cave 16), a monolithic rock-cut temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Pattadakal:**
 
 
• Pattadakal, located in Karnataka, is another UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its blend of Dravidian (Southern) and Nagara (Northern) architectural styles.
 
• The site includes a group of Hindu and Jain temples from the 7th and 8th centuries, built during the reign of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
• The Virupaksha Temple and Mallikarjuna Temple are prime examples of exquisite Chalukyan architecture.
 
 
 
• **Badami:**
 
 
• Badami, also in Karnataka, is famous for its rock-cut cave temples, built during the Chalukya dynasty in the 6th and 7th centuries.
 
• The site includes four main cave temples carved into sandstone cliffs, dedicated to Hindu deities such as Shiva and Vishnu, and one Jain temple.
 
• Badami is also known for its ancient inscriptions and scenic location surrounded by hills and lakes.
